root_cause.text: In `drm_gem_change_handle_ioctl`, a temporary window existed where two IDR entries (old and new handles) referenced the same GEM object without properly synchronizing with a concurrent `gem_close`, allowing the object to be freed and one handle to become a dangling pointer leading to use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "The ioctl briefly had a single object with two idr entries; a concurrent gem_close could delete the object and remove one of the handles while leaving the other one dangling, which could subsequently be dereferenced for a use-after-free." The patch fixes this by first `idr_replace`ing the old handle with NULL before adding the new handle, mirroring the approach in `gem_close` (f6cd7daecff5).

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description states: "The ioctl briefly had a single object with two idr entries; a concurrent gem_close could delete the object and remove one of the handles while leaving the other one dangling, which could subsequently be dereferenced for a use-after-free." The patch fixes this by first `idr_replace`ing the old handle with NULL before adding the new handle, mirroring the approach in `gem_close` (f6cd7daecff5).

candidates.rationale: Declaration of the obj pointer that will be reused in the second IDR entry, allowing two handles to point to the same object.
Declaration of the handle variable used to compute new handle; the new handle is derived from the old handle without additional synchronization.
Acquires prime lock but does not prevent concurrent gem_close from freeing the GEM object, leaving a window for use-after-free.
Locks table_lock to protect IDR operations, but the window for race exists after this lock is released.
Allocates a new handle (handle+1) pointing to the same obj as the old handle, creating a temporary window where two IDR entries reference the object without proper synchronization with gem_close.
Releases the table_lock, after which a concurrent gem_close can free the object while the new handle still exists, leading to use-after-free.
On error path removes the new handle, indicating that the old handle might not be removed in the success path until later, exacerbating the window.

vuln_statements.explanation: Declaration of the object pointer that will be reused for the new handle, allowing two handles to reference the same GEM object without proper synchronization.
Declaration of the handle variable that is used to compute the new handle (handle+1), facilitating the creation of a duplicate IDR entry.
Acquires the prime lock, but does not prevent a concurrent gem_close from freeing the GEM object, leaving a window for use-after-free after this lock is released.
Locks the table_lock to protect IDR operations, but the race window exists after this lock is released and before the object is properly refcounted against gem_close.

Allocates a new handle (handle+1) pointing to the same obj as the old handle, creating a temporary window where two IDR entries reference the object without synchronization with a concurrent gem_close, leading to use-after-free.
Releases the table_lock, after which a concurrent gem_close can free the object while the new handle still exists, allowing use-after-free when the new handle is later accessed.

On the error path, removes the new handle but indicates that the old handle is not removed in the success path, exacerbating the window where two handles point to the same object without proper refcounting.
